brief: September payrolls rose 29,000 against an 84,000 forecast, with August revised down to 133,000 and July negative, pushing October Fed-hike odds from about 75% to 15% while December held near 85%, a postponement rather than a pivot. The 10Y had already risen to 5.33%, its highest since April 2002, on a strong ISM report with prices paid jumping from 71.1 to 77.9, before retracing to 5.18% after the payrolls miss. The piece frames this as demand outrunning available capacity (AI data-center capex, government spend, energy and freight costs) rather than stagflation. Trump's rejection of Tehran's peace proposal, 9,000 additional troops, and continued tanker attacks kept Brent above $100 and prompted a Chinese refined-fuel export suspension and a G7 pledge to release 100 million barrels. French OAT yields rose to about 4.92-4.95%, and the OAT-Bund spread widened past 140bps, the widest since the 2012 euro crisis, on a record EUR340 billion 2027 issuance plan, with contagion spreading into BTPs and the resulting euro weakness driving the dollar to a third straight weekly gain. Equities held near highs on AI strength even as under half of S&P 500 members trade above their 200-day average, leaving the index and the median stock diverging.
